140320601.text: He doesn't seem to notice your approach. Still immersed in his own thoughts, he shakes his head and lets out a long sigh.

140320602.text: (This guy seems promising enough. Maybe I can get some information out of him!)

140320603.text: Hello, sir! Is there anything I can do to help you?

140320607.text: Oh, dear goodness, you're... you're a Marechaussee Hunter!

140320608.text: You recognize us? Ah, are you... one of the people who wrote the commission letter?

140320609.text: Yes, yes! I didn't expect you to actually come. What great news... The city is saved!

140320611.text: Alas... We once lived comfortable, carefree lives. This city used to be free of monsters. The first Marechaussee Hunter, Cassiodor, the "Golden Hunter," he was the one who drove them back.

140320612.text: However... Monsters have once again surrounded the city. Perhaps the seal that kept them at bay has lost its power, or perhaps an evil sorcerer has been meddling in our affairs. All I know for sure is that their return has stripped this city of any chance at peace.

140320613.text: Are there... not enough soldiers to drive them out?

140320614.text: It's not a question of numbers. The guards simply have no idea how to deal with them.

140320615.text: Most people my age have never even seen one of the monsters, much less been trained to fight against them. What's worse, many of us don't even know the history of the Marechaussee Hunters anymore.

140320616.text: When I was a child, though, my grandfather would tell me stories about how the Marechaussee Hunters drove back the monsters. So, on the off-chance that something might come of it, I decided to reach out to you.

140320617.text: To be perfectly honest, I was starting to think all those stories were just tall tales, but now that I've seen you in person, I finally know that it was true!

140320618.text: Well, you can rest easy, friend! The righteous and formidable Marechaussee Hunters are on the case!

140320619.text: The man is touched by your determination and resolve. His eyes begin to well with tears of relief.

140320620.text: Still, if we're going to hunt the monsters, we need to know where to find them. Can you give us any leads?

140320621.text: All I know is that the area outside the city is dangerous. I'm afraid I can't point you toward a specific location.

140320622.text: Although, if you leave the capital through the main gate and follow the road, you should run into a group of guards. They might know more about where to find the monsters.

140320623.text: I see... We'll go look for them, then.

140320624.text: Alright, be careful. Oh and... one last thing. The monsters outside the city are just part of the problem. There are evil sorcerers inside the city as well, so be on your guard.

140320625.text: They're actively working with the monsters, and have corrupted the court ministers with malicious magic. They're the reason why, even inside the city, everything has been a giant mess.

140320626.text: Even one of our kindest ministers has turned into a boorish and unreasonable figure, interested in nothing but enacting laws that exploit the people. Who knows how much longer we'll be able to go on like this...

140320627.text: Talk about being stuck between a rock and a hard place...

140320628.text: I feel bad for him. Maybe we should try to cheer him up?

140320630.text: Hey, not everything can be solved with food!

140320633.text: I appreciate your kindness, but for now, it's more important to focus on the crisis at hand.

140320634.text: Brave Hunters, I leave the future of this kingdom to you.

140320632.text: Huh? Like... now? Is this really the right time...?

140320801.text: If I understood correctly, there are currently two problems in the kingdom that need solving, right?

140320802.text: Exactly. We need to defeat the monsters outside the city and take down the evil sorcerers stirring up trouble from within.

140320803.text: But, which problem should we tackle first...

140320804.text: Well, this seems like a good moment for a break. Take some time, and discuss what you want to do. Let me know when you've made your decision.

140320805.text: Huh... I really didn't expect the people in the city to keep us at arm's length like that. I totally thought the Hunters would be treated like heroes.

140320806.text: Well, Clorinde said the script took cues from the real history of Fontaine, right? Maybe the real-life Marechaussee Hunters were also treated like that?

140320807.text: I wouldn't say it's a perfect representation of history, but there are definitely some similarities. Would you like to hear more about it?

140320808.text: Sure, as long as it doesn't spoil anything in the script! You've brought up bits and pieces of the Hunters' history before, but it was all in passing.

140320809.text: Paimon wants to know, too! The Hunters were super powerful, right? Were they all from a special line of supernatural beings or something? Kinda like... the youkai in Inazuma?

140320810.text: No, all Marechaussee Hunters were ordinary mortal fighters. The only thing that set them apart were the special sword techniques passed down over the centuries.

140320811.text: Huh? So you mean... anyone could become a Marechaussee Hunter?

140320812.text: In theory, yes. All you would need to do is survive the rigorous training, and master the swordsmanship techniques required to fight the monsters.

140320813.text: Still, most people dropped out at the early stages, and others called it quits the minute they saw a monster in person. To become a Hunter, you must be strong in both body and mind.

140320814.text: What kind of monsters did the Hunters fight exactly? Oh and, the "evil sorcerer" the script mentions — did they exist in real life, too?

140320815.text: The land of Fontaine once played host to an ancient dynasty known as Remuria. After that dynasty fell, monsters began to appear, intent on obstructing humans from establishing a new social order.

140320816.text: One of the ancient sorcerers of Remuria used his power to assemble a formidable army of golems. He sought to use that force to establish himself as king.

140320817.text: Now wait a second! Don't tell me that guy was the inspiration for the evil sorcerer in the script! We still haven't found any in-game information on him yet, so why don't you talk about someone else for now?

140320818.text: Well, I wasn't planning on going into anything you might be able to find out in the game... But, if you want me to talk about something else, then... How about Cassiodor, the Golden Hunter, or Egeria, the ex-Hydro Archon?

140320819.text: Wait, but those people are all from a super long time ago! Where did you learn all this, Clorinde?

140320823.text: Absolutely. Ms. Petronilla and my father were good friends. Back in the day, she would often bring Clorinde over to play. But then...

140320824.text: ...Let's not get off topic. Anyway, back to what I was saying...

140320825.text: Responding to Egeria's call, a number of warriors followed Cassiodor into battle against the monsters. This group of warriors, under Cassiodor's leadership, became known as the Marechaussee Hunters.

140320826.text: Yet, as Fontaine entered an era of peace, their work gradually became obsolete. The Marechaussee Phantom, originally an association made up of Hunters, eventually came to be predominantly comprised of Melusines.

140320827.text: Ah, I see... That explains why most of the people in the script have forgotten the Hunters or think of them as nothing more than a legend.

140320828.text: Is that really a bad thing, though? It can get tough always being the one shouldering everyone's expectations.

140320829.text: Hmm, depends on who you ask, I suppose. If the name of the organization no longer commands respect, investigative work is bound to suffer.

140320830.text: Speaking of investigations, which problem should we tackle first? Monsters, or evil sorcerer?

140320831.text: I vote monsters. That's the main duty of the Hunters, right? We can come back to the sorcerer later.

140320832.text: Well said, Miss Furina. Plus, if the sorcerer really are the masterminds behind this whole thing, defeating the monsters could give us some clues on their intentions as well.

140320833.text: What about you, partner? What do you think?

140320841.text: Alright, after some discussion, you decide to turn around and head out of the city...

140320837.text: I mean... you're not wrong. But, those characters are usually the ones pulling the strings behind the scenes. More often than not, they're very formidable opponents. Going after them now might be jumping the gun a little bit.

140320838.text: We don't want a total party kill on the first day, right? With Clorinde as the GM, I wouldn't rule out the possibility...

140320840.text: Haha, then it's settled! Let's go hunt some monsters!

140321801.text: The monsters let out a terrifying roar of anger and resentment, before dissipating into thin air.

140321803.text: We're lucky the Marechaussee Hunter class came with all those preset skill points. Otherwise, we would've been in some real trouble.

140321804.text: I never knew the Fateometer even determines the amount of damage you inflict... If you get unlucky, isn't it just game over right then and there?

140321805.text: Hehe, that's part of the fun! The uncertainty of fate is what gives these games their appeal.

140321806.text: Just as you begin to celebrate your victory, a suspicious lump on the ground catches your attention.

140321807.text: A suspicious... lump? Wait, could it be... the thing that appears after every battle...!?

140321808.text: I walk up to it, crouch down, and begin to carefully examine it. I've still got my right glove on, so it should be fine for me to touch it, right?

140321809.text: As you investigate the mound, you discover that the exposed portion appears to be made of wood. It was previously obscured by the large form of the monsters.

140321810.text: With the monsters gone, the small protrusion now awaits your discovery, poking out of the ground like a shy flower bud.

140330401.text: Looks like everyone's here. Before we begin, why don't we finish where we left off yesterday? There was an important decision to be made, yes? I'll pour everyone a cup of tea.

140330402.text: I—Is that really the most important part, though, Clorinde? Paimon's more concerned about our current surroundings...

140330403.text: Heavy walls, cold railings, dim lights... This is obviously supposed to be a prison!

140330404.text: I admire the work put into the set. Still, it's obvious the script writer has never paid a visit to the Fortress of Meropide.

140330405.text: So this set... is going to be a part of the script?

140330406.text: Unfortunately, that is something I can neither confirm nor deny.

140330407.text: Um, anyone think Clorinde's smile is starting to look kinda scary...?

140330408.text: Well, whatever happens, we'll just have to push on. But first, we should really figure out what to do with this treasure.

140330409.text: If we're worried about arousing suspicion because of our identity... Why don't we give ourselves a different name, just like Clorinde's Master did?

140330410.text: Yeah, it might be better to keep a low profile. As long as we're helping people, it doesn't matter who we are or what we're called.

140330412.text: Staring at me won't get you anywhere. Or, did you want some more tea?

140330414.text: Why aren't you saying anything, Navia? Wait... What's that next to you?

140330415.text: Oh, this is the short sword Clorinde mentioned last night. I found it!

140330416.text: Huh, I'm surprised you managed to track it down after all this time.

140330417.text: Well, I made sure to take good care of it! Considering the... circumstances in which you gave it to me, of course I had to keep it safe.

140330418.text: Anyway, where were we? Oh, right, I was just thinking about all the potential ways for us to break out of prison! We could dig a tunnel, or try to bribe the guards...?

140330419.text: ...Wait, we haven't been thrown into prison yet, have we?

140330420.text: Well, it's only a matter of time! It pays to be prepared, just like how you should always have an umbrella on hand, even when it's sunny.

140330421.text: Alright! Paimon's made up her mind. Let's just give the treasure away!

140330422.text: Paimon may have wanted to keep it, but if that's going to land us in prison somehow, Paimon will be too upset to enjoy her snacks.

140330425.text: So, you've reached an agreement? Alright then, we can continue with the story.

140330426.text: Oh, and we'll collect all the scattered pieces of treasure on the ground as well!

140330428.text: You collect the treasure and make your way back to the capital with your bag of loot in hand.

140330601.text: The city is still shrouded in a gloomy, oppressive atmosphere, but your spirits are surprisingly high.

140330602.text: In places where sunlight struggles to reach, you generously share your wealth with the children, the elderly, and the poor in urgent need of help.

140330604.text: The elderly woman's look of gratitude follows you as you walk away, her eyes never leaving your back until you move entirely out of sight. However, there's still quite a bit of Mora remaining. It appears you haven't made much progress.

140330605.text: (She's probably trying to tell us to speed this up. We need to hurry up so we can address the sorcerer problem...)

140330606.text: Should we go find that man again at the square? He seemed like a pretty responsible guy. I'm sure he knows the people here far better than us.

140330608.text: Just as you start to make way to the square, intent on finding the man again, there's a voice...

140330610.text: Several strange guards suddenly call out to you. They run forward to meet you and proceed to politely pay their respects.

140330611.text: Greetings, gentlemen! Are we being invited for afternoon tea?

140330612.text: Surely, you jest, my lady. That would not be our place. It is His Excellency the king, who requests to meet with you. Please come with us.

140329909.text: As you approach the battlefield, you see numerous people lying by the side of the road. They appear to be dressed like guards.

140329910.text: Their faces are filled with desperation and terror. Some are screaming and cursing in vain, as if still trying to banish the monstrosities they saw from their minds.

140329913.text: The next battle round begins... now.

140339907.text: I'd like to try to hit him with my sword.

140339909.text: Hah, you're facing a veteran Marechaussee Hunter. You don't stand a chance!
